_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Blow the trumpet; the day of the Lord is near.
Even now, return to me with all your heart.
We come with ashes, not to be seen by others.
Create in us clean hearts, O God.
Wash away what we cannot wash ourselves.
Restore to us the joy of your salvation.
Now is the acceptable time; come, let us worship.
We turn toward the cross. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Feel the smudge of ash on your forehead, gritty and dark, the dust we came from and the dust we return to.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
The trumpet is sounding in Zion, not to frighten you but to call you home while the door of mercy stands open.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
So come with everything you have hidden, the fasting no one sees, the tears no one counts; God is gracious and slow to anger.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
Let God create in you a clean heart and a right spirit, and set your treasure where moth and rust cannot reach.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
Now is the acceptable time, friends; now is the day of salvation. Come, let us worship.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross. Lead us home. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Take the ash on your brow: dust, and loved by God.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
Return to the Lord, who is gracious and merciful.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
Create in us clean hearts; restore our joy.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
Now is the acceptable time. Come, let us worship.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross. Amen.
